title: fm board never starts a second board on a port that is still held, and a board it cannot replace is named with its pid and the exact manual step, in English and Chinese
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05, right after T-209 merged, `fm board` ran against a board started before T-209 (pid 32684; state/session/board.json had `code: null`, `owner: null`, `reused: true`). The old board stayed up and kept port 4173, yet `board_start` (bin/fm-herdr.py:2386-2493) took the fresh-start path: `fresh_start` (:2393-2416) decides that the port is free when `http_get(url)` (:2120-2125, a 2 s urllib GET) raises any non-HTTPError OSError, and the old board did not answer that GET in time, so the same OSError meant 'free'. It then launched a second `bun run board/server.ts`, which failed `EADDRINUSE` on 4173 (state/session/board.log), and the only output was `fm board: board did not verify; inspect state/session/board.log` (:2415, printed by main mode 'board', :2843-2847, exit 70). The replacement wait loop (:2443-2449) has the same rule: any non-HTTPError OSError means 'freed'. Separately, a reused board whose board.json has no `code` (a record written before T-203/T-209) never gets a stale notice: the stale branch (:2421) requires `old`, so `fm board` reused it silently although the checkout's code differed. The captain could not tell why the board did not change or what to do.

Held port check. Add `board_listening(port)` in bin/fm-herdr.py next to `board_check_port` (:2333-2345), using the same probe: `socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', port), timeout=2)`; `ConnectionRefusedError` returns False (free); a completed connect returns True; any other OSError (timeout, reset, unreachable) returns True (held: fail safe, never start a second board on doubt). Add `board_port_pid(port)`: when `shutil.which('lsof')` exists, run `lsof -nP -t -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN` with a 5 s timeout and return the first line as an int > 1, else None (any error or no output: None); it never raises. Neither helper prints anything.

Never launch on a held port. In `fresh_start`: keep today's first check (an HTTP response, including HTTPError, means occupied -> today's 'board port belongs to an unverified root' error); when `http_get` raises a non-HTTPError OSError, call `board_listening(port)`; if it returns True, do not launch: raise `BoardRefusal` (below) naming the port and, when `board_port_pid(port)` returns one, the pid. Only when the port is free (refused) does it go on to find Bun and launch as today. After the launch loop, if the board still does not verify and `board_listening(port)` shows the port held by something that is not this child (the child has exited), raise the same `BoardRefusal` instead of 'board did not verify'; the plain 'board did not verify; inspect state/session/board.log' remains only for a child that is still running or a port nobody holds. In the replacement wait loop (:2443-2449), a non-HTTPError OSError counts as freed only when `board_listening(port)` also returns False; otherwise the loop keeps waiting (and ends in today's 'did not stop when asked' notice after ten seconds).

The refusal says what to do. Add `class BoardRefusal(RuntimeError)` carrying `reason = {'en': ..., 'zh-TW': ...}`; `str()` of it is the English text, so existing callers that print `str(error)` stay one line. Texts, with <port> and, when known, <pid>: en `the board on :<port> runs old code or is not answering and cannot be replaced; stop it (kill <pid>) and run fm board` and zh-TW `:<port> 上的看板執行舊程式或沒有回應，無法替換；請停止它（kill <pid>）後再執行 fm board`; with no pid: en `... stop the process listening on :<port> and run fm board`, zh-TW `... 請停止佔用 :<port> 的程序後再執行 fm board`. main mode 'board' (:2843-2847) catches `BoardRefusal` before the generic `(OSError, RuntimeError)` clause and prints two lines, `fm board: <en>` then `fm board: <zh-TW>`, exit 70 (T-209's exit codes unchanged); every other error keeps today's single line. `fm-session start` (report['board'] = board_start(root), :2923) is not changed: it lets the error propagate exactly as today.

A reused board whose code is not recorded is named, not drained. T-209's rule stays: unknown previous code triggers no drain and no `stale` (design.md §11, 'Unknown, dirty or equal checkout code triggers no drain'; pinned by tests/session.test.sh:228-231 and the 'unknown' case at :251 with its assertions at :308-309, which keep every assertion). 'Unknown previous code' means any of: no state/session/board.json (`previous = {}`, bin/fm-herdr.py:2390), a record without a `code` key, or `code: null`. When the board is reused, its previous code is unknown in one of those three ways and the current checkout code is known and clean, `board_start` adds a separate field `code_unknown_reason` = {'en': 'the board on :<port> has no recorded code, so fm board cannot tell whether it runs current code; if it does not show recent changes, stop it (kill <pid>) and run fm board', 'zh-TW': ':<port> 上的看板沒有記錄程式版本，fm board 無法判斷它是否為最新；如果看不到最新的改動，請停止它（kill <pid>）後再執行 fm board'} (no-pid form: 'stop the process listening on :<port>' / '請停止佔用 :<port> 的程序'), with the pid from `board_port_pid(port)`. It sets no `stale`, calls no `board_drain`, kills and starts nothing, and is not saved as a stale flag; main mode 'board' prints its two lines on stderr after the JSON, like the stale notice, exit 0. The existing T-209 'restart it by hand' notices (:2423-2427 drain None or hand-started, :2463-2466 did not stop) keep their wording and gain the pid: en '... stop the board process (kill <pid>) and run fm board', zh-TW '...停止看板程序（kill <pid>）後執行 fm board'; the pid comes from the drain reply's `pid` only when it is valid by the rule the code already applies at :2436 (`type(pid) is int and pid > 1`) and, for the 'did not stop' notice, `os.kill(pid, 0)` still succeeds; otherwise (no pid, `True`, a string, 0, 1, or a dead process) it falls back to `board_port_pid(port)`; with no pid the wording is exactly today's. The phrases the existing tests check ('restart it by hand', '請手動重啟', 'did not stop') stay in the text.

Tests (workers do not run them; evidence is the required GitHub check and the gates), in tests/session.test.sh, using `patch.object` on fm-herdr.py's functions and its own git fixture as the T-209 cases do (never a real board on 4173; no Mock `assert_*` methods in this .sh file, count calls with `call_count` and compare `call_args`, because the fast-checks assertions stage refuses any `assert_<name>` not in tests/lib.sh): (a) held and silent: `board_matches` False, `http_get` raises `TimeoutError` (an OSError), `board_listening` True, `board_port_pid` 4242 -> `board_start` raises BoardRefusal whose en and zh-TW both contain `kill 4242` and `:4173`; lifeline `start` call_count 0; `m.main(['board', repo])` returns 70 and stderr is exactly the two `fm board:` lines. (b) the same with `board_port_pid` None -> the no-pid wording. (c) free port: `board_listening` False -> lifeline start called once (today's behaviour). (d) child exits and the port is held by another process: lifeline start returns a keeper whose poll() is 1, board_matches stays False, `board_listening` True after the launch -> BoardRefusal, not 'board did not verify'. (e) reused board with unknown previous code in each of the three forms (board.json deleted, a record without `code`, `code: null`), current clean code, `board_port_pid` 4242 -> record has `code_unknown_reason` with `kill 4242` in both languages, no `stale`, `board_drain` call_count 0, no kill, no start; `m.main(['board', repo])` exits 0 and its stderr ends with the two `code_unknown_reason` lines. (f) T-209 stale path with old code recorded, `board_drain` None, `board_port_pid` 4242 -> the existing 'restart it by hand' reason now contains `kill 4242` in both languages; and with a drain reply carrying pid 5151 and `session_owned: false` -> the reason names `kill 5151` and `board_port_pid` call_count 0; and in the T-209 'invalid-pid' case (drain pid `True`, :280-281) and 'dead-pid' case (:263-264), with `board_port_pid` patched to 7373, the 'did not stop' reason names `kill 7373` and never `kill True` or the dead pid (add these two assertions inside the existing case loop). (g) replacement wait loop: after SIGTERM `http_get` raises OSError but `board_listening` stays True for the whole wait -> no start, release called, the 'did not stop' notice now naming the pid. (h) `board_listening`: a real closed port (bind a socket, close it, probe its number) returns False; a real listening socket returns True; the case skips on `PermissionError` when binding loopback is not allowed, the way `test_actual_board_start_and_correct_root_reuse` does (:683-687). (i) `board_port_pid` with `shutil.which('lsof')` None returns None and runs nothing. Existing tests keep every assertion and only gain patches so nothing touches the real machine: tests that simulate a free port with `http_get` raising OSError also patch `board_listening` to return False, and every test that reaches a stale or unknown-code notice also patches `board_port_pid` (return None, so their exact-text assertions see today's no-pid wording) - namely `test_board_code_notice_uses_its_own_git_fixture` (:166-231: `board_listening` False in its fresh block :180-190, `board_port_pid` None for the whole test so its stale block :205-215 and unknown-code loop :225-229 run no lsof; :214-215's exact stderr assertion compares stale lines only and the unknown-code loop never calls main, so both stay as they are), `test_board_drain_replacement_preserves_session_and_waits_for_free_port` (:233-324: `board_listening` False, paired with its `get` side effect at :268-275 so each 'freed' OSError is also refused; `board_port_pid` patched per case: 7373 for the 'invalid-pid' and 'dead-pid' cases (asserted in (f)), None for every other case; the 'unknown' case at :251 still asserts drain call_count 0 and no `stale` at :308-309; the 'hand' and 'timeout' drain replies carry the valid live `pid: 900`, so their reasons now name `kill 900` while the existing substring checks ('restart it by hand', 'did not stop when asked', :316) still pass, and the 'hand' case's `killed.call_count == 0` (:322) stays green because the `os.kill(pid, 0)` liveness check applies only to the 'did not stop' notice, never to the hand-started notice), and `test_board_start_goes_through_the_lifeline_owned_by_the_session` (:656-678). `test_board_reuse_does_not_spawn_and_wrong_root_is_refused` (:153-165) and `test_main_board_mode_reports_in_one_line_never_a_traceback` (:612-631, its subprocess case runs on FM_PORT=1 with no Bun: port 1 refuses, so 'board requires Bun' stays) need no change and stay green. `test_actual_board_start_and_correct_root_reuse` (:679-760) uses a real free port and stays green.

Callers, checked by grep: `board_start` is called only by main mode 'board' (:2845) and session start (:2923); `fresh_start` is local to it; `http_get` keeps its contract (other callers unchanged); no other file imports these helpers (tests/session.test.sh imports fm-herdr.py as `m`). `board_check_port` (:2333, used by `fm setup`, :2838) is unchanged.

Docs, edited in place (T-189: nothing appended at the end of design.md): design.md §11 'Managed session defaults', the paragraph that begins 'Board reuse is verified with a fresh random file' (about :2815-2836): add that a port counts as free only when a TCP connect is refused, so a listener that does not answer the root check in time is never mistaken for a free port; that `fm board` then names the board's pid and the manual step (`kill <pid>`, then `fm board`) in English and Chinese with exit 70; that a reused board whose code is unknown (no record, no `code` key, or `code: null`) is still not drained but gets a bilingual notice naming its pid; and that the restart-by-hand notices name `kill <pid>` when the pid is known.

In flight. board.json keeps T-209's fields and may gain the optional `code_unknown_reason`; no stored record is rewritten. A board.json already on disk without a code (any of the three unknown forms) now gets the code-unknown notice on `fm board` instead of silence, and still no drain. A board running today (recorded code, post-T-209) behaves exactly as T-209 defined unless its port stops answering in time. The one board this would have caught (pid 32684) is already replaced by hand. Running autopilot and worker rounds are not touched (the change is in fm-herdr.py's board functions only; the autopilot reloads per T-203 after merge).

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7. Fail-first: cases (a), (b), (d), (e), (f), (g), (h), (i) are red on base (the helpers, BoardRefusal and `code_unknown_reason` do not exist, base launches on a held port, stays silent on unknown code, or names no pid); (c) and the adapted existing tests keep their assertions unchanged, but they are red on base too, only because they patch `board_listening` / `board_port_pid`, which do not exist on base (`patch.object` without `create=True` raises AttributeError); their assertions are the regression guards, and on head they are green. The fail-first gate needs only some red assertion (bin/fm-failfirst.sh:424-427), which (a), (b), (d)-(i) provide. No vendor stub is involved; lsof is never run for real in the tests except through `shutil.which` patched to None or the `board_port_pid` function patched.
